what_its_for: This medicine is a liquid protein solution given directly into your vein (IV). It provides your body with the building blocks of protein, called amino acids, when you cannot eat enough food by mouth or through a feeding tube. It is used to help your body heal, maintain muscle, and stay nourished during illness, surgery, injury, or other medical conditions that prevent normal eating.
how_to_take: This medicine is always given by a trained healthcare professional (nurse, doctor, or pharmacist) through an IV line into your vein. You will NEVER inject or take this medicine yourself at home without proper training and a doctor's close supervision. It is usually mixed with other nutrients such as sugars, fats, vitamins, and minerals before it is given to you. The IV bag will drip slowly into your vein using a pump that controls the exact speed. Never try to speed up or slow down the drip on your own. Tell your nurse right away if you notice swelling, pain, redness, or leaking around the IV site.
dosing: Your dose is carefully calculated by your doctor and pharmacist based on your weight, medical condition, kidney and liver function, and how much protein your body needs each day. A typical adult may receive between 1 and 2 grams of amino acids per kilogram of body weight per day, but your dose may be higher or lower. This medicine is given continuously over many hours, or sometimes around the clock, depending on your treatment plan. Your healthcare team will adjust your dose regularly based on blood tests and your progress. Do not adjust the IV pump rate on your own.
missed_dose: Because this medicine is given in a hospital or clinic by healthcare professionals, missed or interrupted doses are managed by your medical team. If your IV line becomes blocked, disconnected, or the bag runs empty, tell your nurse or caregiver immediately. Do not try to restart the infusion yourself. Your care team will reschedule or adjust your nutrition as needed to make sure your body gets what it needs.
storage: This medicine is stored and handled by the pharmacy and medical staff. If you are receiving this at home under medical supervision, keep the IV bags in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C and 8°C). Take the bag out of the refrigerator and let it reach room temperature (about 1 to 2 hours) before use. Never freeze the bag. Use each bag only once. Do not use a bag that looks cloudy, has particles floating in it, or has changed color. Check the expiration date on the label and never use it after that date. Keep all bags in their original packaging away from direct light until ready to use.
what_to_avoid: Do not eat or drink anything beyond what your doctor has specifically allowed, as your nutrition is being carefully managed through this IV solution. Avoid touching the IV needle, tubing, or connection ports to reduce the risk of infection. Do not let anyone other than trained healthcare staff handle the IV equipment. Avoid activities that could pull or dislodge your IV line, such as sudden arm movements or rough play. Do not add any medicines, vitamins, or other substances to the IV bag unless a pharmacist or doctor has specifically approved it, as mixing can cause dangerous reactions.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or go to the emergency room right away if you notice any of the following: fever, chills, or shaking (which may be signs of infection); redness, swelling, warmth, or pus around your IV site; difficulty breathing or shortness of breath; chest pain or a fast or irregular heartbeat; sudden headache, confusion, or dizziness; swelling in your hands, feet, ankles, or face (which may mean you are retaining fluid); nausea, vomiting, or severe stomach pain; high or low blood sugar symptoms such as extreme thirst, frequent urination, shaking, sweating, or feeling faint; yellowing of your skin or eyes (which may be a sign of liver problems); or any unusual or severe reaction that worries you.
when_it_works: This medicine starts working as soon as it enters your bloodstream. Your body uses the amino acids right away to build and repair tissues and support important body functions. You may not feel an immediate difference, but over days to weeks your doctor will check blood tests to see that your protein levels and nutritional markers are improving. Recovery time varies depending on your underlying illness, how malnourished you were before treatment, and your overall health.
special_populations: Older adults may need lower doses and closer monitoring of kidney and liver function and fluid levels. Children and newborn babies (especially premature infants) require specially formulated pediatric amino acid solutions and very precise dosing calculated by a specialist; adult formulas are generally not appropriate for infants without specific medical guidance. If you are pregnant or breastfeeding, your doctor will carefully weigh the benefits and risks before prescribing this treatment. People with kidney disease may need reduced doses or special formulas to avoid buildup of waste products. People with liver disease need careful monitoring because the liver processes amino acids. Always tell your entire healthcare team about all your medical conditions and all medicines, vitamins, and supplements you are taking.
